newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S official dismisses spat with Paris over Africa.
newsitem.headline: U.S official dismisses spat with Paris over Africa.

text.p: Senior U.S. diplomat George Moose, in Paris for talks with French officials, dismissed past major disagreements with France over Africa policy and said the two Western powers were in broad agreement.

"This is one of those questions like, "When did you stop beating your wife,'" Moose, who is U.S. assistant secretary of state for African affairs, told Reuters when asked if Paris and Washington had put behind them a diplomatic spat over Africa which broke out last year.

"There has always been more agreement amongst us than there has been a difference, and that remains true today," Moose said after talks with French Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain, the first Franco-American talks at such a senior level since last year's tiff.
Moose, who also held talks with Foreign Ministry and foreign aid offials as well as an adviser to French President Jacques Chirac, said the day's meetings had been "very, very good".
Paris and Washington bickered openly last year over U.S. participation in a multinational humanitarian assistance mission to aid refugees in Zaire.
They also fought publicly over Washington's motives for sending U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on a tour of Africa shortly before last year's U.S. presidential election.
Godfrain said at the time it was only when black American voters were about to go to the polls that Washington showed an interest in Africa.
Washington angrily complained at the charge.
Chirac said last week that rivalry between outside powers for influence in Africa should be a thing of the past.
"The time is no longer right for rivalries which harken back to another age," Chirac told Paris-based diplomats at a New Year ceremony.
